points: Yechezkel can't speak, so Hashem has him deliver the message through three symbolic acts.
He draws Yerushalayim under siege on a brick, then sets an iron plate between it and himself: Hashem won't listen to the people now.

He lies on his left side 390 days and his right side 40 days. The Metzudas David reads these as years of sin; the 40 are Yehuda's years after the 10 tribes were exiled, when they still did not change.
He lives on tiny rations of bread and water (under 1,000 calories a day), a public picture of the coming starvation.

When we lost prophecy, we lost a way of connecting to Hashem through imagination and emotion, not only the mind. Rav Kook says this returns as the end of days nears, and Torah music and art are a sign of it.
